mechanism: Intention-to-treat analysis preserves the prognostic balance created by randomization by analyzing participants according to their originally assigned treatment group, regardless of nonadherence, crossover, or treatment discontinuation. It estimates the effect of treatment assignment rather than efficacy among adherers.
vignette: A randomized trial compares two medications. Some participants stop their assigned medication, and others cross over to the alternative treatment. Investigators want the primary analysis to preserve the benefits of the original randomization and estimate the effect of treatment assignment.
lead: Which analysis strategy is most appropriate?
correct: Analyze participants according to their originally randomized groups regardless of treatment actually received
distractors: Analyze participants according to the treatment they ultimately received
Exclude all participants who did not fully adhere to the assigned treatment
Analyze only participants who completed every follow-up visit and remained adherent
Reassign crossover participants to a new group after the crossover occurs
distractor_notes: An as-treated analysis breaks the original randomized comparison because treatment received can be influenced by prognosis and other post-randomization factors.
A per-protocol/adherers-only analysis can introduce selection bias by excluding participants based on post-randomization behavior.
A complete-case adherent analysis combines exclusions for missingness and adherence and does not preserve randomization.
Reassigning participants after crossover converts the analysis into a treatment-received/time-dependent comparison rather than preserving original random assignment.
key_expl: The intention-to-treat principle analyzes participants according to their randomized assignment, even if they discontinue, switch, or incompletely adhere to treatment. This preserves the causal interpretation of randomization for the effect of treatment assignment. Per-protocol and as-treated analyses answer different questions and can be biased by post-randomization selection.
objective: Apply the intention-to-treat principle by retaining participants in their originally randomized groups despite crossover or nonadherence.
